claim: GeoComply positions itself as 'Compliance, KYC, growth and anti-fraud under one roof' and its named product suite consists of six products: GeoComply Core (geolocation compliance/anti-fraud), IDComply (KYC/AML), PinPoint (on-property geofencing), GeoGuard (VPN/proxy detection), GeoComply Chargeback Integrator (GCI), and OneComply (licensing/compliance management). No promotion administration, wallet/ledger, or marketing product exists in the enumerated suite.
page_title: GeoComply | Compliance, KYC, growth and anti-fraud under one roof
notes: Suite enumeration corroborated by the solutions page and 2023 gaming brochure PDF; used as the basis for reasoned 0 scores in unrelated matrix sections (A, F).

claim: Homepage scale claims: 2+ billion transactions processed monthly, 200+ million trusted users, 99.9999% uptime, 'up to 7 figures in monthly fraud savings'.
page_title: GeoComply | Compliance, KYC, growth and anti-fraud under one roof
notes: Uptime figure differs from the 99.999% claimed in the 2026 Brazil press release; treat 99.9999% as marketing.

claim: GeoComply Core verifies user location at device level using GPS, Wi-Fi, cellular (GSM) and IP signals; supports SDKs for desktop, mobile apps and web browsers; processes transactions 'in milliseconds'; 1.2 billion geolocation checks monthly; 99% transaction pass rate; provides 'one dashboard' for transaction analysis, fraud hotspot geofencing, and 'enhanced troubleshooter messages'.
page_title: GeoComply Core | Get Compliance-Grade Geolocation
notes: Official product page; 'troubleshooter' is GeoComply's reason-code/messaging system also referenced in operator help centers and third-party integration writeups.

claim: Core runs 'hundreds of location data, device integrity, and identity fraud checks on every geolocation transaction' (elsewhere quantified as 350+ checks), detecting jailbroken/rooted devices, fake location apps, emulators, VPN/proxy/Tor, GPS spoofing, location jumping, proxy betting, and account sharing.
page_title: GeoComply Core | Get Compliance-Grade Geolocation
notes: 350-check figure also appears on the GCI product page.

claim: GeoComply operates a 'Flexible Rules Engine' with dynamic real-time capabilities: a new rule added roughly every 18 hours, ~28,000 accumulated data integrity conditions, machine learning models for multi-accounting, bonus hunting, account takeover and synthetic ID fraud; data 'crunched in milliseconds'.
page_title: Geolocation intelligence that can't be beat | GeoComply
notes: The rules engine is vendor-operated detection logic; no evidence it is exposed to customers as an authorable policy engine.

claim: GeoComply's fraud solutions include 'customizable autoblock capabilities with rule configuration matching individual risk tolerance', multi-user device reports, bonus-hunter location reports, and a global high-risk location dashboard for monitoring fraud hotspots.
page_title: Bolster Your Compliance Program with Geolocation Intelligence | GeoComply
notes: Shows operators can configure blocking rules/risk thresholds; depth of configurability not documented publicly.

claim: Integration model ('client collects, server decides'): the client-side SDK gathers an encrypted geolocation payload and returns a transaction reference; the operator backend exchanges per-environment API key/secret for a short-lived license token, submits the encrypted packet to GeoComply's server-side decryption API, and receives a structured result containing resolved state/jurisdiction code, an allow/block decision, and reason codes (the 'troubleshooter') that operators map to deny/retry/re-check logic.
page_title: GeoComply Integration: 14-Step Production API Setup [2026] - Tech Insider
notes: Official integration docs (integrationdocs.geocomply.com) are authentication-gated and the subdomain did not resolve from this research environment; details taken from search-corroborated third-party integration writeups and are consistent with official marketing ('troubleshooter', SDK model).

claim: SDK coverage: native iOS 16+ and Android 10+ SDKs; desktop (Windows 10+, macOS 12+) requires installing the GeoComply Player Location Check (PLC) plugin, with the browser JavaScript SDK talking to it over a local WebSocket bridge (default port 54321). SDK binaries and credentials are issued through an onboarding pack tied to the operator's license - there is no public package-manager distribution.
page_title: GeoComply Mobile SDK: iOS & Android in 15 Steps [2026] - Tech Insider
notes: Platform list consistent with official 'SDKs for desktop, mobile apps, and web browsers'. GeoComply's GitHub org has only ~4 public repos (e.g., truelocation-browser-ios-public); developer access is license-gated, i.e., not a self-serve developer platform.

claim: IDComply is an 'all-in-one KYC & AML solution': verifies personal details (DOB, address, name, SSN) against authoritative sources; supports photo ID + selfie checks, knowledge-based authentication from credit records, phone/mobile-carrier and email validation; screens PEP, OFAC, HIO, sanctions lists and criminal records in real time; addresses multi-accounting, bonus abuse, identity theft and account takeover.
page_title: All-in-one KYC/AML solution for fraud prevention | IDComply
notes: Official product page.

claim: IDComply operates a per-jurisdiction compliance engine: 'waterfall logic verifies data through multiple sources and automatically checks every subsequent source until a successful verification is achieved'; it verifies customers 'with customizable fields that meet each jurisdiction's compliance rules', supports state-specific requirements (e.g., KBA mandated in certain U.S. states), and relieves operators of 'tracking regulatory changes' for KYC across jurisdictions.
page_title: All-in-one KYC/AML solution for fraud prevention | IDComply
notes: Jurisdiction-specific KYC rules are encoded and maintained by GeoComply as a managed service, not exposed as customer-authorable policy.

claim: IDComply received full licensing approval from the New Jersey Division of Gaming Enforcement (DGE) as a KYC (age and identity verification) solution for iGaming, supporting KBA or digital identity secondary authentication; operators manage geolocation and identity 'through a single back-office and API'.
page_title: IDComply Solution for KYC Licensed in New Jersey | GeoComply
notes: Official press announcement; demonstrates the vendor itself is licensed/approved by gaming regulators and that geolocation + KYC share one back office.

claim: IDComply pass-rate claims: 'up to 95%' first-try verification across 46 U.S. states (2023), ~90% in Ontario, 'up to 20% higher than that of individual vendors'; a single API call runs the entire multi-vendor waterfall.
page_title: AML & KYC Solutions for iGaming | IDComply
notes: Vendor-reported performance figures.

claim: IDComply commercial and orchestration model (2023 brochure): 'No integration or licensing fees. One single price, multiple verification sources. No monthly or annual volume commitment. No minimum spend.' GeoComply handles all KYC vendor procurement and relationships; partners provide data verification, KBA, phone identity verification, and ID photo verification; IDComply stores only anonymized Player Identifiers.
page_title: An Integrated Cybersecurity Solution for Geolocation, Anti-fraud & KYC iGaming (GeoComply brochure PDF)
notes: Text extracted directly from the official brochure PDF. This is cross-vendor identity signal orchestration/normalization behind one API - the strongest J06-adjacent evidence.

claim: GeoGuard detects VPNs, proxy servers, Tor exit nodes, hosting providers, P2P networks, Smart DNS proxies, hijacked residential IPs and 'proxy over VPN'; database of 310+ million IPv4/IPv6 addresses with continuous (up to hourly) updates; claimed 98% detection accuracy (99.6% in an earlier brochure); deployable as cloud API, on-premise download, or pre-integrated at the edge with Amazon CloudFront and Akamai; includes a real-time rules engine with machine learning; marketed as 'Hollywood Studio-approved'.
page_title: GeoGuard | VPN and Proxy Detection Solution | GeoComply
notes: Used for streaming geo-piracy, gaming, financial services and sanctions compliance.

claim: GeoGuard is pre-integrated with Amazon CloudFront and can be deployed 'turn on and go' through AWS Marketplace; case study: MultiChoice blocked unauthorized VPN viewing monthly and roughly doubled supported concurrent live-stream users.
page_title: Protecting streaming services using GeoComply | AWS Media Blog
notes: AWS-published partner case study; also the only quasi-self-serve distribution channel found for any GeoComply product.

claim: PinPoint provides custom on-property geofencing combining beacon technology with compliance-grade geolocation, 'accuracy down to 1 meter', differentiating indoor/outdoor betting for on-property compliance.
page_title: Geolocation Solutions to Fight Fraud | GeoComply Products
notes: Niche product for casino-property use cases.

claim: GeoComply Chargeback Integrator (GCI) generates 'compelling evidence reports in 60 seconds or less' from historical geolocation data spanning '6 months to 2 years' plus 350+ device integrity checks; reports are 'accepted by 70+ payment processors' and aligned with Visa Compelling Evidence 3.0; supports bulk case creation/processing and claims to cut dispute handling time by up to 90%.
page_title: GeoComply Chargeback Integrator (GCI) | GeoComply
notes: Demonstrates retained historical location/device records queryable per user/transaction and packaged as dispute-grade evidence - the strongest D-section and J07-adjacent evidence.

claim: Official brochure: chargeback reports carry 'extremely precise timestamps on user activity and their location... robust enough to win disputes from banks'; customer quote (Omer Sattar, Sightline Payments): 'GeoComply cut our payment fraud costs by at least 85%... The anti-fraud reports were literally good enough to take to the bank in order to win our chargeback disputes.'
page_title: An Integrated Cybersecurity Solution for Geolocation, Anti-fraud & KYC iGaming (GeoComply brochure PDF)
notes: Vendor-published customer quote; supports evidence-grade historical reconstruction of user location/device state, not of policy/rule versions.

claim: OneComply centralizes gaming licensing and compliance: onboard information once into a data repository and 'instantly assemble signature-ready licensing applications for business and key employees across multiple jurisdictions' (USA and Canada); proprietary 'OmniFill' technology auto-inserts repository data into jurisdiction-specific application forms; claims to reduce gaming disclosure filing redundancies 'by an astounding 97%'.
page_title: License Application & Management | Our Solutions | OneComply
notes: OmniFill naming corroborated by SBC Americas coverage (2022). This is licensing-workflow automation, not rule/policy management.

claim: OneComply License Control tracks employee/business/product licenses and certifications with dashboards, task assignment, due-date tracking and automatic notifications; 'alerts when changes to a company's business or personal disclosures require the submission of a material change report' and 'automatically prompts to create a compliance task with suggested lead times for filing'; provides 'audit reporting for regulatory compliance reviews' and secure file sharing with investigators and regulators; 'gaming regulators are utilizing OneComply for investigations and application submission'; security features include AES-256 encryption, IP whitelisting and 2FA.
page_title: License Control | Our Solutions | OneComply
notes: Composite of OneComply solutions pages (license-control, license-application-and-management, onecomply.com/solutions). Workflow/approval surface is for licensing filings and personnel compliance, not for deploying decision rules.

page_title: GeoComply acquires leading licensing platform provider OneComply
